newsitem.title: USA: Russian Mars probe to land in the sea -U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: Russian Mars probe to land in the sea -U.S. official.

text.p: The disabled Russian space probe will land in the Pacific Ocean 500 miles (800 kms) southeast of New Zealand, posing no danger to people, a senior White House official said on Sunday.
"There is no danger to anyone and that is very good news," U.S. National Security Council official Robert Bell told CNN.
Bell said the impact zone was calculated on the last orbit the six-tonne spacecraft made before re-entering the Earth's atmosphere.
The official said the U.S. Space Command's entire satellite network was focusing on the spacecraft and would get a very good fix on its re-entry.
He said the Space Command would be able to localise the impact to a few miles within 15 minutes of impact.
Bell said the Mars probe was travelling at 17,000 miles (27,400 km) per hour and the parts of it that did not burn up on re-entry would strike Earth within minutes.
